subject: Private deployment evidence & operator transfer playbook — CardioHealth procurement questions
messages:
From: Jill Hoffman <jill@cardiohealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow up: private deployment evidence and operator access questions

Sofia — thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has a few follow-ups before we can sign the Order Form for the on-prem deployment. A short list below so legal and ops can verify we’re aligned:

- Can Redwood provide a tamper-evident snapshot transfer procedure and an attestation letter from your engineering team that the snapshot represents the customer-owned data and runtimes at the point-in-time transfer?
- For operator access: we need a written boundary describing what Redwood operators can and cannot do post-deployment (e.g., emergency support, break-glass read-only, remote troubleshooting).
- Evidence of audits/attestations (SOC2 or equivalent) and a brief sample of the runbook you’d hand over for day-2 ops.

We appreciate any attachments; procurement would like to review and then route to our legal counsel. Timeline: ideally by the end of this week.

Thanks,
Jill Hoffman
Head of Procurement — CardioHealth
(attachment: cardio-soc2-questions.pdf)

Team — forwarding CardioHealth’s procurement list. They want a snapshot transfer procedure + operator boundary + sample runbook. Can you draft the minimal evidence bundle and a short attestation that legal can sign off on?

My suggestions: attach a trimmed runbook (no sensitive keys), an operator-handback checklist, and a short technical attestation (1 page) that describes snapshot integrity and verification steps. Suggest we offer a third-party verifier option for the snapshot handover (they often ask for escrow-like assurance).

Constraints: we should avoid sending private keys or any PII. If we must include a live snapshot, propose a transfer protocol that uses an S3 presigned URL under mutually agreed retention and an HMAC checksum for integrity verification.

Karthik — can you own the technical description and checklist? Marcus — can you flag any legal wording we should pre-empt (e.g., "custody", "operator access", "runbook delivery timeframe")?

Thanks,
Sofia
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: request-from-cardio.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow up: private deployment evidence and operator access questions

Sofia / Marcus — putting together the tech-side proposal. High level (we can tidy for legal):

1) Snapshot transfer process (minimal viable package):
   - We produce an encrypted VM image + Redwood runtime tarball + metadata manifest (model version, image hash, timestamp).
   - Transfer happens via customer-controlled S3 bucket or mutually accessible secure transfer (SFTP/TLS). We provide a presigned, time-limited link and an HMAC-SHA256 checksum for verification.
   - We recommend including a short integrity test script and the manifest verifying checksums.

2) Attestation wording (draft bullet points):
   - "Redwood Engineering certifies that the delivered snapshot represents the service runtime and configuration in effect on <timestamp>. Redwood has not included any customer PII in the snapshot artifact. The integrity of artifacts is protected by HMAC and SHA256 checksums."

3) Operator boundary (proposed):
   - Redwood operators will not have ongoing administrative credentials in the customer environment post-handover.
   - Emergency support: break-glass access is available only with a documented request and bilateral approval; access is time-limited, logged, and audited.
   - Read-only remote diagnostics are possible via an agent that sends telemetry to a customer-owned endpoint; no credentials are stored by Redwood.

4) Evidence bundle (what we attach to Procurement/Legal):
   - trimmed runbook (operations runbook without secrets) — redwood-privdeploy-runbook-v1.3.pdf
   - operator-handback-checklist.xlsx — lists steps for snapshot export, handover, and verification
   - short attestation letter (1 page) — technical wording above (we'll produce a PDF)

5) Optional third-party verification: we can coordinate with an independent custodian (e.g., a neutral S3 escrow or notary service) to take custody of the snapshot for a limited window and attest to the transfer. That usually satisfies enterprise procurement that wants an "escrow-like" mechanism without full escrow.

I'll prepare a cleaned package and a single-page attestation. Marcus — any legal flags?

—Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: operator-handback-checklist.xlsx)

Hi Jill / CardioHealth procurement — thanks for the clear list and quick timeline. Attached is a concise evidence package that addresses your asks: a trimmed runbook, an operator handback checklist, and a proposed attestation. High-level notes below and next steps:

- Snapshot transfer: we propose using your S3 (preferred) with a presigned upload window (we provide the presigned PUT and an HMAC checksum). If you prefer a neutral custodian for escrow-like verification, we can engage a third-party notary; please advise if you have a vendor preference.
- Operator boundary: Redwood will not retain admin credentials after handover. Emergency break-glass can be requested via an authorized ticket and will require joint approval; any session is logged and delivered to your security team.
- Runbook & attestation: attached runbook is sanitized (no keys). The attestation includes the checksum value and the timestamp format we will use.

Attachments: redwood-privdeploy-runbook-v1.3.pdf; operator-handback-checklist.xlsx; Redwood-attestation-Cardio-20260615.pdf (draft).
